display.title: Episode 231: The Stolen Purse
display.summary_short: Before summer vacation, Uncle Yossi asks listeners to recruit new Tzivos Hashem soldiers, and tells how a servant's loyalty to the Rebbe of Chortkov was blessed with great wealth.
display.summary_long: With summer vacation coming, Uncle Yossi encourages Tzivos Hashem soldiers to tell new friends and relatives they meet on their travels about Hashem's army, so that many soldiers will greet Moshiach. After the Hakochainik march, an eleven-year-old boy who wrote asking to be a guest says the Shema in Studio 604 and tells what he learns. The story: the Rebbe of Chortkov, known for his generous tzedakah, finds before Pesach that the purse of 500 gold coins set aside for the poor is gone. Only his trusted servant, Meir Anshel, has a key, and to the Rebbe's shock Meir Anshel says he took it and soon returns the money. Then a Polish count summons the Rebbe and hands him the original purse: a cleaning maid had stolen it. Meir Anshel admits that he never took it; he gave his own savings so the poor would have Pesach. The Rebbe blesses him with success, and Uncle Yossi says he was Meir Anshel Rothschild, whose five sons became great bankers known for their tzedakah. The show ends with a sponsor message and more names in the Sefer Torah contest.
display.lesson: Care for others even at your own expense; kindness and honesty bring Hashem's blessing.
